title: Intertrigo & the flexural differential
summary: Inflammation of opposed skin folds from friction, heat and moisture. It is a description, not a diagnosis: sort out candida, tinea, erythrasma, flexural psoriasis and seborrhoeic dermatitis before reaching for combination creams.

glance.think: A red, moist, sore rash under the breasts, in the groin, armpits or abdominal folds, especially with obesity, diabetes or incontinence.
glance.engine: Skin-on-skin friction plus trapped sweat causes maceration; yeast and bacteria colonise secondarily.
glance.backbone: Dry and separate the folds (cotton, moisture-wicking textiles), barrier products, short mild steroid; treat confirmed candida or erythrasma specifically.
glance.never_miss: Flexural psoriasis, extramammary Paget disease, and erythrasma or tinea treated as ‘simple intertrigo’.

what: Superficial **inflammation of opposed skin surfaces** (flexures/folds) driven by heat, moisture, friction, and poor evaporation. May be purely irritant or complicated by yeast/bacteria; often overlaps inflammatory dermatoses (psoriasis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, contact allergy).
cause: Occluded flexures trap sweat → maceration → barrier failure → inflammation ± overgrowth of resident flora (*Candida*, Corynebacteria, dermatophytes, Staph/Strep). Risk: obesity, diabetes, hyperhidrosis, immobility, incontinence, tight synthetics, hot/humid environments. Infant napkin dermatitis is a related fold problem.

list: Erythema, itch/burn, moist/macerated skin, fissures in crease depth, peeling.
Sites: inframammary, axillae, groin, abdominal apron, natal cleft, neck, finger/toe webs.

**Day 2 case:** 50-year-old; 3-month itchy red **symmetrical inframammary** rash; smooth surface, well-defined borders, mild peripheral scale; **KOH negative**; on HRT; no other sites or new topicals → diagnosis **intertrigo** (inflammatory/irritant-predominant).

features: Secondary infection clues: satellite pustules (candida), foul odour (Gram-negatives), honey crusts (impetigo), coral-red Wood lamp (erythrasma).
diagnosis: Clinical. KOH/mycology if scale, satellites, or treatment failure; bacterial swab if pustules/crust/odour; consider patch testing if allergen suspected; biopsy if atypical or refractory (granular parakeratosis, Hailey–Hailey, etc.).
differentials: Day 2 KOH-negative picture still overlaps early inverse psoriasis and seborrhoeic dermatitis — reassess if not settling with dry-care + mild steroid.

differentials: Tutor end-week takeaway: when treating flexural rashes, **keep dry**, address incontinence/sweating/obesity, and **screen secondary bacterial/fungal infection**.
management: **Cornerstone — keep dry and reduce friction** (tutor end-week emphasis):

list: Shower after sweating; **dry folds thoroughly** (cool hairdryer useful under breasts/axillae).
Loose natural-fibre clothing; address incontinence and obesity where relevant.
Barrier pastes (e.g. zinc oxide) for weepy irritant folds; avoid irritating talc as primary strategy.
Mild topical corticosteroid short course (e.g. **hydrocortisone 1%** 1–2 weeks) for inflammatory intertrigo once infection unlikely/treated.
If candida likely or empiric after failed dry-care: topical azole (± mild steroid combo products used cautiously in primary care).
Bacterial secondary infection: topical or oral antibiotic per local guidance.
Avoid potent/very potent steroids in folds (atrophy, striae, rebound).

management: Further management (Day 2): follow-up response; if persists → repeat mycology/culture; reconsider inverse psoriasis, contact allergy, seborrhoeic dermatitis; review HRT/medications only if clinically relevant contributors.
red_flags: Rash that fails to clear in one fold, especially in an older adult: biopsy for **extramammary Paget disease**.
Spreading redness, pain and fever: cellulitis.
Repeated ‘intertrigo’ that relapses as soon as treatment stops: think **inverse psoriasis** (see the [psoriasis](condition:psoriasis) page).
pearls: KOH negative ≠ “never fungal” — sampling error and mixed pictures exist; re-test if course atypical.
Combination clotrimazole–HC / similar: pragmatic in primary care but reassess if no clear infection signs and no improvement.
Counsel that **prevention** (dryness) beats endless cream cycles.
